title: What goosebumps are trying to do 🥶
subject: skin
description:
What gives you goosebumps every time? 👇

Why do we get goosebumps when we're cold, scared or hear a great song? Tiny muscles pull every hair up, a reflex left over from when our ancestors had fur.

Sources: BrainFacts.org / Society for Neuroscience ("What Causes Goosebumps?"), Harvard Stem Cell Institute (Shwartz et al., Cell, July 2020), Science News

scenes.text: Your skin is puffing up fur you don't have.
Almost every hair has a tiny muscle, and cold, fear or a great song pulls them up.
On furry animals, it traps warm air and makes a cat look bigger.
We lost that fur, so it barely helps. But here's the strange part.
In 2020, Harvard researchers found that nerve also wraps hair stem cells in mice, and long cold makes them grow hair.
